title: Tensor pool aging and cudaMadvise experiments
body:
Purpose
----
Notes from experiments investigating an unusual OOM tail on p4d clusters where GPU memory graphs show a persistent set of small "ghost" blocks that never get reclaimed even after model unloads. Hypothesis: alignment-padding + tensor pool aging interacts poorly with our slab allocation buckets and cudamallocasync deferred free path; cudaMemAdvise (readMostly/migratable hints) changes eviction behavior and can reduce fragmentation in specific workloads.

Context & why this matters
----
- Customer workloads exhibit intermittent OOMs at 95th percentile load despite total allocated working set well under GPU capacity.
- Reproduces more often on mixed-size requests (small prompt-only jobs interleaved with long-context generation).
- Existing notes (see parent folder) cover allocator sizing, retry patterns, and slab contention; this doc explores a different angle: allocation alignment and memory advice interactions with tensor pools and eviction heuristics.

Observed symptoms
----
- Post-load memory map (ptmalloc-like mempool telemetry) shows many 256B/512B allocations in high-count bins scattered across the GPU heap.
- After workload spike, some of these small blocks remain marked "reserved" in our mempool but are not reachable by any active tensors — they appear as "ghost blocks" in heap dumps taken via CUPTI + custom heap snapshots.
- cudaMallocAsync fallback logs often show decommit/retry cycles around the same timestamps as the ghost block growth.
- cudaMemGetInfo shows available memory dropping in small increments rather than large contiguous chunks, implying fragmentation rather than sustained working set growth.

Hypotheses (short)
----
1) Alignment padding: many intermediate tensors have shapes that cause allocation sizes to round up to the next alignment boundary (e.g., 64->256 bytes due to internal rounding), creating a lot of small-sized dead space when tensors are short-lived.
2) Tensor pool aging: our tensor pool keeps recently freed buffers in per-stream caches to avoid expensive cudaMalloc work; however, aged entries are not coalesced and remain in fragmented slots that cannot satisfy larger allocations.
3) cudaMemAdvise behavior: marking pages with certain advice flags (readMostly/migratable) changes their placement or eviction priority causing allocator free-lists to be split across different memory regions, preventing defragmentation.
4) CUDAMallocAsync deferred free ordering: interplay between deferred frees and our slab reclamation timer creates transient peaks of small allocations that get pinned and never merged.

Experiments run (summary)
----
Experiment A — alignment profile:
- Add fine-grained telemetry to capture requested size vs actual allocated size (post-alignment) across a 24h production-like load replay.
- Result: ~42% of allocation events for short-lived activations had effective allocated size >=4x requested due to padding to nearest 256B slab boundary and 64B vector alignment.
- Actionable: consider reducing min-bucket-size for small tensors or introduce fast path for <64B tensors to use pooled tiny arenas.

Experiment B — pool aging aggressive purge:
- Introduced a config flag to purge per-stream caches aggressively after N seconds of inactivity (N=5s, 30s, 120s runs).
- Observed: with 5s purge, ghost block count dropped ~63% and tail OOM frequency decreased on replay. However this increased effective cudaMallocAsync churn and led to ~7% higher average allocation latency.

Experiment C — cudaMemAdvise toggles:
- Marked long-lived KV cache buffers with cudaMemAdvise(..., cudaMemAdviseSetReadMostly) and separately tried cudaMemAdviseSetPreferredLocation targeting host vs device (on unified memory tests).
- Observed: readMostly hint reduced page migration but increased cross-stream fragmentation because hints caused allocator to segregate pages by advice type. PreferredLocation hints had no benefit on dedicated GPU (no host migration) but affected unified memory staging tests.

Experiment D — deferred-free ordering adjustment:
- Adjusted the flush ordering of cudaMallocAsync deferred frees to batch by size class instead of FIFO.
- Observed: coalescence improved slightly; ghost blocks that were contiguous in size class were reclaimed more often, decreasing fragmentation fraction on traces where the workload had size locality.

Repro steps (how to reproduce locally)
----
1) Use p4d.24xlarge or similar with cuda11.8+ and CUDAMallocAsync enabled.
2) Run the provided replay harness (linked_artifacts PR 894) which simulates mixed prompt+gen traffic with variable sequence lengths.
3) Enable allocator telemetry: set environment REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE=1, REDWOOD_SMALL_BUCKET_CUTOFF=256.
4) Start run for 1 hour and snapshot heap every 60s using our snapshotter (see PR).
5) Compare "requested_size" vs "actual_alloc_size" histogram, and measure ghost-block persistence by tracking blocks freed but not reused for >120s.

Key logs/metrics to check
----
- allocator.free_list_state and per-bucket occupancy over time (timeseries)
- cudaMallocAsync fallback counts (+ timestamps)
- resident_page_retention per arena and per-stream cache sizes
- heap_snapshot: block.id, size_requested, size_actual, last_used_ts
- SLO impact:  p50/p95 allocate latency before/after purge changes

Root cause thinking so far
----
- Not purely slab-size misconfiguration; alignment rounding is a major contributor (many allocations are small but align up to 256B which is too coarse for workloads with many 32–100B temporaries).
- Tensor pool aging preserves many small buffers that are unlikely to be reused for large allocations; because they are scattered across arenas, they fragment the heap and prevent contiguous free regions.
- cudaMemAdvise can unintentionally increase logical fragmentation by introducing a second dimension (advice tag) which we currently treat as opaque; allocator ends up splitting free lists by advice state.

Short-term mitigations (safe, low-risk)
----
- Reduce min-bucket alignment for tiny allocations (experiment toggle): lower from 256B to 64B for transient tensors, gated by a flag. Risk: increased free-list management overhead but likely net win for these workloads.
- Add a periodic background coalescer that attempts to scan neighboring free blocks and coalesce across per-stream caches (low frequency, e.g., 1/min).
- Add a telemetry alert rule: when fraction of small orphaned blocks > 8% for >5 minutes, trigger auto-purge of per-stream caches.

Medium-term changes (requires more validation)
----
- Partition arenas by allocation lifetime hints: have short-lived arena(s) optimized for tiny temporaries and long-lived arena(s) for KV caches; allocation pathways choose arena based on tensor lifetime prediction (heuristic by op type).
- Update deferred-free batching to group by size class and arena adjacency to improve coalescence probability.
- Treat cudaMemAdvise tags as an explicit allocator dimension (i.e., do not mix advice-tagged pages with general-purpose arenas unless coalesced).

Open questions and unknowns
----
- How does multi-tenant noisy-neighbor behavior amplify these effects when arena affinity spreads across customer slices?
- Does lowering min-bucket-size significantly increase allocation CPU overhead under peak throughput? Need microbenchmarks.
- Are there CUDA driver-level behaviors (hidden heuristics) that change on different driver versions (we saw different fragmentation patterns on 11.7 vs 11.8 in a couple runs)?

Next steps / Action items
----
- [Marco] land telemetry PR (done, PR 894) and run 72h replay with reduced small-bucket setting in canary pool.
- [Aisha] run microbench allocation CPU overhead tests for min-bucket 64B vs 256B on p4d/gtx cluster. Deadline: 2025-11-15.
- [Dana] prototype arena-partition by predicted lifetime; simple heuristic: activations created by attention/ffn ops -> short-lived arena. Prototype deadline: 2025-12-01.
- [Luis] write a test harness to reproduce cudaMemAdvise split behavior across advice toggles and capture allocator free-list fragmentation metrics.

Notes to self / informal observations
----
- We saw a weird case where a single request with many tiny logits tensors caused fragmentation that persisted for ~9 minutes; looks like an allocation stampede where pool cached a large number of similarly sized blocks that never matched later request shapes.
- There are trade-offs: purging caches aggressively fixes fragmentation but increases allocation latency and kernel stalls; need a smart, workload-aware policy.
- Slack thread includes a screenshot of heap snapshot coloring by advice tag — that highlights the problem visually (linked in linked_artifacts).

References
----
- Internal: PR 894 allocator telemetry and small-bucket experiment.
- Related notes in sibling files: several fragmentation investigations in this folder (see file list) — this doc intentionally focuses on alignment/pool-aging/madvise interactions rather than allocator internals already covered elsewhere.

Unresolved TODOs
----
- Add flame graphs for allocation CPU in the replay.
- Instrument cross-stream reuse rates for tiny buckets.
- Validate behavior across driver 11.7/11.8/12.x matrix.

End of note.
